finding.claim: The subject= check is silently skipped when the token has no sub claim, so a caller requiring a specific subject accepts tokens that have none.
finding.source: Token payload: an attacker holding any validly signed token from the same issuer that omits sub (e.g. minted for another purpose or audience with the same key).
finding.sink: Application's subject-based authorization decision after jwt.decode(..., subject=...) returns.

trace.note: _validate_claims calls _validate_sub when verify_sub is enabled (default True).
`if "sub" not in payload: return` exits before the subject argument is checked.
Subject comparison runs only when the claim is present, so an absent sub never matches the required subject.
Inconsistent with _validate_iss, which raises MissingRequiredClaimError when issuer is requested and iss is absent.
Inconsistent with _validate_aud, which raises MissingRequiredClaimError when audience is requested and aud is absent.

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification runs first and cannot be bypassed (api_jws.py:277-285), so the token must be validly signed by the trusted key. require=["sub"] would block this but is opt-in. The sub-must-be-string check (api_jwt.py:449-450) runs only when the claim is present.

finding.claim: A token with a missing or unknown kid forces an unthrottled, uncached outbound JWKS fetch on every request before any signature check, amplifying load on the JWKS endpoint and blocking a worker for up to the 30 s timeout.
finding.source: Unauthenticated token header: kid may be absent or any random string (read from the unverified header at jwks_client.py:224-226).
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP GET to the configured JWKS URI (urllib.request.urlopen at jwks_client.py:118), with refresh=True bypassing the cache.

trace.note: get_signing_key_from_jwt decodes the unverified header and reads kid (None if absent).
Passes the attacker-supplied kid to get_signing_key.
Lookup against cached keys fails for unknown or None kid (match_kid compares equality only).
No match triggers get_signing_keys(refresh=True): no rate limit, no negative cache, no backoff.
refresh=True makes data None so fetch_data() performs a live HTTP request.
urlopen with timeout=self.timeout (default 30 s, line 26), before the token's signature is checked.

finding.guards_checked: URI is fixed by the application and restricted to http/https (jwks_client.py:77-82), so this is not SSRF and the attacker cannot change the target. kid is used only for equality matching against trusted keys, so no injection or key confusion. Signature verification still happens afterwards. Keys without kid are excluded from signing keys (jwks_client.py:174-178), so a None kid cannot match.
